anchors.note: Attacker-controlled string str is consumed to compute len (string length) and num_elements (colon count + 1). For the PoC input, len is a small value determining loop bounds.
23-byte stack buffer allocated without initialization. All bytes are indeterminate. Only explicit writes (character accumulation and null termination) will make specific bytes defined.

Characters from the input string that pass the alphanumeric/dash/underscore check are written into buf one at a time. For the PoC, only a small number of characters are accumulated before the '+' delimiter is encountered, leaving buf mostly uninitialized.
On encountering '+', the buffer is null-terminated at position buf_used. Bytes buf[0..buf_used] are initialized (characters plus null), but buf[buf_used+1..22] remain uninitialized.

Guard only checks that buf_used is non-zero (at least one character written). No check that buf_used >= strlen("ECDSA")=5, so any token shorter than 5 characters proceeds to strcmp with partially uninitialized buf.
